question: A kangaroo ran 150 m in the first 40 seconds and then, it ran 100 m in the next 10 seconds. Still, its displacement was only 50 m. The average speed of the kangaroo is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**5 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The kangaroo covered a total distance of 150 m + 100 m = 250 m.
 
• The total time taken by the kangaroo is 40 s + 10 s = 50 s.
 
• Average speed is calculated as the total distance divided by the total time.
 
• Thus, the average speed = 250 m / 50 s = 5 m/s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Distance**: It refers to the total path covered by an object. It is a scalar quantity and only has magnitude.
 
• **Displacement**: It is the shortest distance from the initial to the final position of an object. It is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.
 
• **Speed**: It is the rate at which an object covers distance. It is a scalar quantity and is given by the formula: Speed = Distance / Time.
 
• **Average Speed**: It is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. It gives a general idea of how fast an object is moving overall.
 
• **Velocity**: It is the rate of change of displacement. It is a vector quantity and is given by the formula: Velocity = Displacement / Time.
 
• In this context, although the displacement of the kangaroo is only 50 m, for average speed calculation, the total distance covered (250 m) is considered.
